transcript.text:
Thank you both — these are exactly the constraints I needed before settling. Let me summarize what I'm hearing so we can confirm the design direction.

From compliance (Mina): audit records must be retained immutably for exactly 7 years and encrypted with a customer-managed key. This means our storage layer must enforce immutability and integrate with customer-managed key management regardless of which pipeline pattern we choose.

From data platform (Theo): the billing service can only emit audit events reliably through a transactional-outbox-to-Kafka pattern — direct publishing or a managed queue won't work for that service. This effectively rules out direct Kafka publishing and a managed cloud queue as viable options, since the pipeline must serve all services including billing. Additionally, the pipeline needs exactly 12 Kafka partitions to handle expected peak load.

Given these constraints, the transactional-outbox-to-Kafka design is the only option that satisfies all services. Before I settle, are there any other constraints or concerns from either side that we haven't surfaced yet? If not, I'll record the final design with: transactional-outbox-to-Kafka architecture, 7-year immutable retention, customer-managed key encryption, and 12 Kafka partitions.

commitments.detail: Configure Kafka with exactly 12 partitions to handle expected peak load.
Ensure Kafka-level retention settings and any tiered storage are consistent with 7-year immutable retention and CMK encryption requirements before production.
Ensure long-term storage layer enforces immutability and integrates with customer-managed key management for 7-year retention.
All services including billing must adopt the transactional-outbox-to-Kafka pattern for emitting audit events.
